display_title: Global Markets Rebound Ahead of Earnings
short_summary: World markets showed signs of stabilization following a turbulent week, as investors braced for major tech earnings and evaluated economic indicators from Asia.

sources.name: Globes
sources.title: מגמה מעורבת באסיה, וול סטריט מתאוששת לקראת שבוע של דוחות

paragraphs: Global financial markets staged a tentative recovery following a turbulent week, providing investors with much-needed breathing space ahead of an intensive schedule of corporate earnings. On Wall Street, futures tied to the S&P 500 advanced 0.2%, while Nasdaq contracts rose 0.4%, recovering from Friday's retreat. This rebound followed a steep downturn in semiconductor equities, where the benchmark SOX index suffered its longest consecutive daily losing streak since 2006. Investors are now bracing for crucial tests concerning whether mounting artificial intelligence spending can be justified, especially as bond yields climb and financing costs become increasingly burdensome.

Trading across the Asia-Pacific region painted a mixed picture. Japan's Nikkei 225 dropped 0.8%, and the MSCI Asia Pacific index surrendered 0.6% after earlier trimming losses, whereas South Korea's Kospi climbed 0.6%. Equity benchmarks in Shanghai and India's Nifty remained flat. Regional sentiment was anchored by China, where third-quarter gross domestic product accelerated by 4.5%, exceeding expectations. Although this robust expansion reinforced confidence that Beijing could attain its official annual growth target, it simultaneously dampened expectations for subsequent state economic easing.

Energy markets also reflected moderated tension. Brent crude retreated 1.7% to approximately $108 per barrel, backing away from a five-month peak despite persistent geopolitical escalation in the Middle East. Meanwhile, the Tel Aviv Stock Exchange commenced trading without obvious catalysts for optimism, having advanced 4% the prior week amid receding domestic inflation. Nevertheless, economists largely anticipate interest rates will remain unchanged, disappointing hopes for rate cuts. Compounding the pressure, dual-listed shares exhibited sharp negative arbitrage gaps, led by chipmakers Tower, Nova, and Camtek, alongside Palo Alto Networks, which faced an anticipated drop exceeding 8% following a steep selloff among cybersecurity peers.

In New York, quarterly reports promise crucial visibility into technology sector health. Tuesday brings earnings from streaming giant Netflix and SpaceX, followed Wednesday by Meta, which faces strict scrutiny over whether immense artificial intelligence expenditures are generating tangible revenue and operating profit. Reports from Western Digital, Lam Research, and Texas Instruments will further clarify baseline industry demand for semiconductors.

Looking further ahead, prominent macro investor Paul Tudor Jones—famed for anticipating Wall Street’s historic 1987 Black Monday crash, which marked its thirty-ninth anniversary as the Dow Jones plummeted 22.6%—warned that American equities could confront severe headwinds by 2027. Jones plans to establish short positions then, citing a structural shift in supply rather than corporate earnings deceleration. An impending wave of mega initial public offerings, potentially featuring private artificial intelligence pioneers OpenAI and Anthropic, alongside insider share sales and lockup expirations, threatens to saturate the market. According to Goldman Sachs projections, American offerings could raise $675 billion in 2026 and $600 billion in 2027. Jones cautioned this capital-absorptive dynamic could reverse years of shrinking share supply driven by buybacks, drawing unsettling parallels to the challenging 1998–2002 market era.

facts.fact: Asian stock markets displayed mixed performance, with Japan's Nikkei 225 sliding 0.8%, South Korea's Kospi advancing 0.6%, and the MSCI Asia Pacific index shedding 0.6%.
China's gross domestic product expanded by 4.5% in the third quarter, surpassing expectations.
Brent crude slipped 1.7% to approximately $108 per barrel, retreating from a five-month high.
Futures on the S&P 500 rose 0.2% and Nasdaq futures climbed 0.4% following a difficult week where the semiconductor SOX index suffered its longest losing streak since 2006.
Upcoming corporate earnings reports include SpaceX, Netflix, Meta, Western Digital, Lam Research, and Texas Instruments.
Billionaire hedge fund manager Paul Tudor Jones voiced concerns regarding equity headwinds in 2027, citing an impending surge in public offerings.
Goldman Sachs projects equity capital raising through IPOs and follow-on offerings in the United States will reach $675 billion in 2026 and $600 billion in 2027.
